text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Opposition parties Pro Patria, the Rightwing and the Moderates demanded early parliamentary elections in 1997 after continued quarrelling in the ruling coalition and a badly compiled budget, party leaders said.
- The director of the Police Department Ain Seppik said he and Border Guard Chief Tarmo Kuuts considered resigning because of a lack of funds for their departments in the 1997 budget.
- The leader of the Reform Party parliamentary faction, Valve Kirsipuu, avoided in an interview a direct answer to the question whether the party would continue in the coalition.
- Estonia and Latvia cannot trade fishing quotas because the fishing agreement was not signed by the agreed deadline September 1.

- Polls show the leading candidates for the post of the mayor of Tallin are Toivo Jurgenson from Pro Patria, Priit Vilba from the Reform Party, Kalev Kallo from the Centre Party and Robert Lepikson from the Coalition Party.
- Parliament intends to pass last-minute amendments to the election law, simplifying clarification of results in the constituencies where only independent candidates stand.
- Estonian and Ukrainian Chambers of Industry and Commerce signed an agreement to cooperate.
